anchor_definition: The anchor is the function exported as `encrypto` (minified `s`): it parses a fixed AES key, AES-ECB/Pkcs7 encrypts the input, and rewrites the base64 to the URL-safe form actually seen in the `words` field. PLAN §5.1: the dedicated value-constructing function is the anchor, not the translate handler that calls it (too generic, just assigns the result) nor CryptoJS AES (a reusable primitive).

anchor.why: AES-ECB(Pkcs7) encrypt of the input with the fixed key 4e87183cfd3a45fe, then base64 made URL-safe (/ -> _, + -> -). This produces the exact `words` token value observed in the translate request.

roles.why: The translate-action handler: trims the input, calls encrypto(e) and assigns it to i.words, then dispatches getTranslate(i). It triggers the request but only forwards to the encryptor.
`decrypto`: the inverse transform (URL-safe base64 back to standard, AES-ECB decrypt). Not on the request-construction path.
